methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series E → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.4x) to $15.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $2.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Divergent
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series E), post-money $2.3B

data.narrative:
Fairmat is a Series E robotics and manufacturing company that has raised approximately €95M ($103M) to date. The valuation analysis relies on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms and one public comparable, with three primary peers at the same or adjacent stage: Divergent (Series E, $2.3B), Exotec (Series D, $2.0B), and Locus Robotics (Series F, $2.0B).

Two methods were applied to triangulate value. The Stage-Progression method uses a $15.0B total-raised proxy as a base and applies a typical 1.4x step-up multiplier for Series E progression, implying a $21.0B valuation. The Peer-Median method across the three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $2.0B implied value, with the peer range spanning $2.0B to $2.3B. The substantial divergence between these approaches reflects methodological differences in how growth trajectory and peer-relative positioning are weighted.

The triangulated analysis implies a valuation range of $1.7B (low) to $24.1B (high), with a median of $11.5B. The wide band reflects material uncertainty around whether Fairmat's capital efficiency and stage progression align more closely with typical private-market peer multiples or justify a significant premium. Resolution requires clarity on revenue scale, unit economics, and customer concentration relative to the peer set.
